title: Thin shell thickness identification from a cantilever frequency
source: Euler–Bernoulli cantilever beam theory (Timoshenko and Young, Vibration Problems in Engineering): f1=beta1²/(2 pi L²) sqrt(EI/(rho A)), beta1=1.875104068711961. For a unit-width strip with I=b t³/12 and A=b t, f1=beta1² t sqrt(E/(12 rho))/(2 pi L²). The tolerance also bounds the measured 8-to-16-element mesh change and the closed-form first-mode Timoshenko shear/rotary correction.

quantities.reason: The independent thin-strip target is t=0.005 m. The 8-element frequency is 0.006994825643627156 Hz and the 16-element frequency is 0.006994839209354149 Hz, a relative mesh difference of 1.939390826041693e-06. The first-mode Timoshenko correction below is 5.416830989868338e-06; their sum is 7.356221815910031e-6, rounded upward to the stated 7.4e-6 relative tolerance.

The closed relation is linear in t; with 1e-5 Hz independent error, sigma_t=1e-5/(f1/t), and the endpoint is t-1.959963984540054 sigma_t. The 4e-8 m allowance is the 7.4e-6 model-discrepancy budget applied to t=0.005 m, rounded upward.
The same thin-beam linearization gives t+1.959963984540054 sigma_t. The 4e-8 m allowance is the 7.4e-6 model-discrepancy budget applied to t=0.005 m, rounded upward.

The Euler–Bernoulli reference is 0.00699489012460471 Hz. The 8/16 mesh difference is 1.939390826041693e-06 relative and the first-mode Timoshenko shear/rotary correction is 5.416830989868338e-06; their sum is rounded upward to 7.4e-6.
